basis: Sean, 2026-10-29: "take a stab at reasonable decisions for the items that require my input". Claude reviewed every decision flagged for Sean. Anything not listed under calls was accepted as built.

verdicts.changed: Changed: a follow-up build carries it out
verdicts.needs-you: Kept for Sean: a serious concern or his own earlier call
verdicts.deferred: Deferred: waits on work Sean postponed

D52.note: A signed-in device should renew its own session with its device key, so the account password is asked only on a new device, after a remote sign-out, or after 30 days without use. Today a session lasts 8 hours with no renewal, so a device that syncs all day asks for the password again. Built by slice 32 (#25, D400–D408).

D138.note: Crown jewels (wallet phrases, recovery codes) are left out of locked backups unless opted in one by one. If the account and the server are both lost, a restore brings back everything except the most valuable items. Recommendation: put crown jewels in locked Lockdown backups by default, sealed under the backup password, and keep them out of plain exports as your D121 says.

D210.note: Keep the silent passkey upgrade, and add a notice afterwards ("github.com added a passkey to this login") on the item and as a toast, so nothing is saved without the person ever hearing about it. Built by slice 33 (#26, D410).

D229.note: A push relay that Lockdown runs for self-hosted servers is an ongoing service with a running cost. It waits for the native mobile apps, which you deferred under D122.

D230.note: Strength words: weak under 50 bits, fair 50 to 74, strong from 75. The default 6-word passphrase (77.5 bits) then reads strong, as it is, instead of fair. Built by slice 33 (#26, D412).

D307.note: Kept on by default. This takes back the system-wide shortcut you listed as deferred in D122; it was kept because it needed no OS-level integration. Ctrl+Shift+Space matches 1Password's quick access.

D312.note: Same notice as D210 after an upgrade that follows a password you typed yourself. Built by slice 33 (#26, D410).

D328.note: A split view stays a warning for the vault, which keeps reading and syncing, but it pauses new contact look-ups, new shares and emergency-access grants through that server until the split clears. A server showing two histories is the moment it could swap someone's keys. Built by slice 33 (#26, D413).

D346.note: Built by slice 29 (#21): the line on Security in the desktop app, the web vault and the CLI.

D371.note: The link to the device is kept. The proposed "Revoke it on Devices" hint is left out: a device that is waiting usually just needs updating, and a nudge to revoke could cost someone a device they still use.

D442.note: The status lines as built; the plural forms read naturally.

D443.note: Show then Copy keeps a code off the screen until asked, matching the app.

D444.note: Bringing the window forward reveals nothing; the app still asks for its own unlock.

D455.note: Sean asked for it after his first run on the Mac.

D456.note: The words say plainly that the file opens the account with the password, and where to keep it.

D459.note: A4 suits most of the world but not a US printer. The PDF uses US Letter where the system's region uses it (US, Canada, Mexico, the Philippines and the rest of the Letter regions) and A4 elsewhere; the first-run slice carries it, since it rebuilds the kit screen.

D482.note: Everything Lockdown keeps on the device, found by the app's identifier and its own data folder; a guard refuses anything near the top of the disk or above the home folder.

D483.note: The shared identity is erased only when no other app is named in it, so a reset can't take Mailbird's or Synapse's keys with it.

D487.note: Every kind and the edge cases Sean asked for; password age isn't checked by Watchtower yet, so 'old passwords' waits on that.

D488.note: Records Sean's Q5 call: the demo opens from first run with no account, a bar on every screen, and Leave the demo.

D466.note: The master password through --master-password-stdin, LOCKDOWN_MASTER_PASSWORD or a prompt. One follow-up: lockdown init without --name still makes a passwordless install for old scripts; that should become a refusal or a prompt, so a command-line-only install is sealed too.

D473.note: The move copies everything and switches only once it's all there; a failed move leaves the vault as it was.

D475.note: What Sean asked for: comfortable is roomier by default, compact by setting, all tokens.
